The Python exit-code consumer was updated to use `_ALERTING_DRIFT_CLASSES` (line 584) but the workflow consumer of the same JSON wire shape was not, so the two consumers now disagree on whether dangling alerts.
advisory.finding: The canary CI workflow still counts `dangling` as an alerting drift class, contradicting the change's new contract that `dangling` is informational and must never alert. `_ALERTING_DRIFT_CLASSES` in bridge_fsck.py excludes `dangling`, and the exit-code comment states dangling 'must NOT gate the exit code, else windowed absence goes red forever, unhealable' — but the workflow consumer of the same `bridge_fsck --output json` shape was not updated: its `cells` tuple includes `dangling`, so a non-empty `dangling` still sets `drift_found=true` and opens/keeps-open the `binding-drift-alert` ticket the in-process exit code deliberately suppresses.
scenarios: A binding with persisted `absent_404_count>0` produces a `dangling` entry; the in-process bridge-fsck exit code stays 0 (non-alerting) but the canary workflow opens/keeps a binding-drift-alert bug open on the same run.
The stated f436 goal — 'empty binding_drift is satisfiable' / no forever-red — is only met for the CLI exit code, not for the canary alert ticket which still fires on dangling.
